# A Go target with no way back to the thread it draws on refuses the program
# rather than emitting a call that freezes the window. The unit test in
# internal/lower says the refusal happens; this says it survives the CLI as a
# diagnostic a person can act on -- the file, the line and the column of the
# call, and the name of the platform that has to change.
#
# android under Go is that platform today: its Go is a library the Kotlin
# screen calls, and nothing in it reaches the main thread. gtk4 has an idle
# tick, and bubbletea a message Update runs, and both take the same program.

! sngl generate --lang go --platform android --out out app.sngl
stderr 'app\.sngl:13:\d+:'
stderr 'this call blocks'
stderr 'android has no way to run anything back on the thread it draws on'
! exists out

sngl generate --lang go --platform gtk4 --out out2 app.sngl
grep 'go func\(\) \{' out2/model.go
grep 'gtk4rt\.Post\(func\(\) \{' out2/model.go

sngl generate --lang go --platform bubbletea --out out3 app.sngl
grep '__snglPost\(func\(\) \{' out3/model.go

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import go "sngl:language/go"

#[go.native("time", "time.Sleep")]
#[go.async]
func sleep(ns int)

component main node {
    var greeting = "idle"

    text #out(value=greeting)
    button #load(text="load", @click {
        sleep(300000000)
        greeting = "done"
    })
}

window {
    main
}
